mainTopic: The snake and others who wanted what was not theirs lost what they had; then the גמרא begins asking for the source of the משנה's rule that a סוטה's punishment starts with the thigh.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about people who wanted what was not theirs. The נחש הקדמוני wanted חוה, did not get her, and lost his kingship, his upright walk and his human food. Ten more people from תנ״ך followed the same pattern. The גמרא then asks how we know the סוטה's punishment starts with the thigh. אביי explains that the curse names the thigh first, while the water works belly first, and the כהן warns her of that order so no one doubts the water. A new משנה teaches מידה כנגד מידה: שמשון and אבשלום were punished to match their sins, while מרים, יוסף and משה were rewarded to match their good deeds, and ה׳ Himself gathers in every צדיק. The גמרא then expands on שמשון: his sin with his eyes, his downfall beginning in עזה, דלילה weakening him, and several teachings on the פסוקים of his birth and early strength. The amud ends just as רבי חמא ברבי חנינא begins to explain 'והוא יחל להושיע את ישראל', and his words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: The original snake wanted what was not his
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings the נחש הקדמוני as another example of someone who wanted something not fitting for him. He did not get it, and he lost what he had.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same thing happened with the original snake. He set his eyes on something that was not fitting for him. So he did not get what he wanted, and what he already had was taken away.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds the snake from גן עדן as one more example of the rule just taught about the סוטה. She wanted what was forbidden and lost what she had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern has two parts: what he asked for was not given, and what he had was taken away. The next steps will show both parts from the פסוקים of the snake's curse.

keyTerms.meaning: And so we found: introduces another example of the same pattern
The original snake, the one in גן עדן
Not fitting for him, not his to have

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the סוטה to a big principle of how ה׳ punishes: someone who grabs for what is forbidden ends up losing what he already had.

phrases.english: And so we found with the original snake,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנָּתַן עֵינָיו בְּמַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לוֹ —
phrases.english: that he set his eyes on what was not fitting for him —
what he asked for, they did not give him,
and what was in his hand, they took from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous part of the daf, which taught this pattern about the סוטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who desires what is not fitting for him does not get it and loses what he had. The snake is the classic example.

steps.title: What the snake lost: kingship, walking upright, and human food
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ says what He had planned for the snake: king over the animals, walking upright, and eating human food. Each one is turned around by a phrase in the curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ said: I planned for him to be king over all animals, and now he is 'cursed more than all cattle and beasts of the field.' I planned for him to walk upright, and now 'on his belly he shall go.' I planned for him to eat human food, and now 'dust he shall eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves the second half of the pattern, 'what he had was taken away.' It reads each phrase of the snake's curse as the loss of something good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the curse in בראשית is matched to a blessing the snake was supposed to have. Instead of ruling over the animals, he is cursed more than all of them. Instead of walking upright, he crawls. Instead of eating human food, he eats dust.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I said he would be king
over every domestic and wild animal,
and now "he is cursed
more than all the cattle and all the beasts of the field."
I said he would walk upright,
now — "on his belly he shall go."

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי יְהֵא מַאֲכָלוֹ מַאֲכַל אָדָם,
phrases.english: I said his food would be the food of people,
now — "dust he shall eat."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי יְהֵא מֶלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows from the פסוקים the claim of step 1 that what the snake had was taken from him.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the snake lost what he already had.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The curse of the snake in בראשית 3:14, read phrase by phrase.

steps.title: What the snake wanted and did not get
steps.stepSummary: The snake planned to kill אדם and marry חוה. Instead, ה׳ put hatred between him and the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: The snake said: I will kill אדם and marry חוה. Now the פסוק says: 'I will put hatred between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves the first half of the pattern, 'what he asked for was not given.' The snake wanted חוה, and instead got hatred between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step reveals what the snake was really after: getting rid of אדם and taking חוה. The punishment is the exact opposite of his plan. He gets hatred between himself and the woman, not closeness.

phrases.english: He said: I will kill Adam
and marry Eve,
now — "I will put hatred between you and the woman
and between your offspring and her offspring."

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא אָמַר אֶהֱרוֹג אֶת אָדָם וְאֶשָּׂא אֶת חַוָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the snake example by showing the other half of the pattern: what he wanted was not given.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the snake did not get what he desired.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 3:15, hatred between the snake and the woman.
steps.whatToRemember: The snake is the model case: he wanted חוה and did not get her, and he lost his kingship, his upright walk and his good food.

steps.title: Ten more people who wanted what was not theirs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists קין, קרח, בלעם, דואג, אחיתופל, גחזי, אבשלום, אדוניהו, עוזיהו and המן. All of them followed the same pattern as the snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same happened with קין, קרח, בלעם, דואג, אחיתופל, גחזי, אבשלום, אדוניהו, עוזיהו and המן. They set their eyes on what was not fitting for them. What they wanted was not given to them, and what they had was taken from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes by showing that this pattern repeats all through תנ״ך, with a list of ten people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list adds no new reasoning. It shows that the rule is general and not limited to the snake or the סוטה. Each person grabbed for something like power, כהונה, kingship or money, and ended up losing what he had.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's big lesson: whoever reaches for what is not his loses both what he wanted and what he had. The סוטה, the snake and these ten people all show it.

phrases.english: And so we found with Cain, Korah, and Balaam,
and Doeg, Ahithophel, and Gehazi,
and Absalom, Adonijah, Uzziah, and Haman —

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנָּתְנוּ עֵינֵיהֶם בְּמַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לָהֶם.
phrases.english: that they set their eyes on what was not fitting for them.
What they asked for was not given to them,
and what was in their hand was taken from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the snake example to many other people, closing the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pattern of losing both what you wanted and what you had applies to many people in תנ״ך.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the thigh is punished first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that the סוטה began her sin with the thigh, and asks for the source of this order.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'With the thigh she began the sin,' and so on. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה: her punishment starts with the thigh because her sin started there. It asks where this order comes from in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the thigh is struck first and then the belly. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows this exact order.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? It asks for a source.

phrases.english: "With the thigh she began the sin," etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. The rest goes on: and afterward the belly, so the thigh is struck first.

phrases.english: From where do we know these things?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and returns to explain a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that shows the thigh is struck before the belly.

steps.title: One פסוק says thigh first, another says belly first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the כהן's oath, which mentions the thigh first. It then challenges this with the later פסוק, which mentions the belly first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the source is the פסוק 'When ה׳ makes your thigh fall and your belly swell,' there is a problem. Another פסוק says, 'Her belly shall swell and her thigh shall fall.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible source and immediately attacks it. The two פסוקים list the body parts in opposite orders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק, the oath the כהן says, puts the thigh first, which fits the משנה. But the פסוק describing what actually happens to her puts the belly first. So we cannot simply prove the order from the first פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: offers a possible answer that is about to be challenged
But isn't it written: brings a פסוק that seems to contradict

steps.confusionAlert: The word אילימא signals that the suggested source will not hold up as it stands. It is not the גמרא's final answer. אביי resolves the problem in step 7.

phrases.english: If you say it is because it is written:
"When ה׳ makes your thigh fall away
and your belly swell" —
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:21. These are the words the כהן says in the oath.

phrases.english: but isn't it written:
"And her belly shall swell and her thigh shall fall away"?
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:27. This פסוק describes what actually happens to her, and here the belly comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the question of step 5 and immediately challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that במדבר 5:21 proves the thigh is struck first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: במדבר 5:27 lists the belly first, so the order in the פסוקים is contradictory and cannot prove the משנה's sequence.

steps.title: אביי: the curse goes thigh-first, the water checks belly-first
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that both פסוקים are right. The curse names the thigh first, but the water physically checks the belly first.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When the כהן curses her, he curses the thigh first and then the belly. But when the water checks her, it checks along its natural path: belly first, then thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the problem from Step 6. Each פסוק describes a different thing: one is the curse, the other is the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 found two orders: thigh-then-belly in the oath, and belly-then-thigh later. אביי says the thigh-first order belongs to the spoken curse, and that is the source that her sin began with the thigh. The belly-first order is simply the path the water travels inside the body.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When he curses, he curses the thigh first,
phrases.notes: "He" is the כהן saying the curse to the woman.

phrases.english: and afterward he curses the belly.
But the water, when it checks her,
checks according to its path:
belly first, and then thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי לָיֵיט — לָיֵיט תְּחִילָּה יָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two פסוקים into two different subjects: the curse versus the water's action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The belly-first פסוק seemed to cancel the thigh-first proof
steps.terutzMaskana: The curse names the thigh first, which is the source; the water just works in its physical order

steps.title: But the curse itself also says belly first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: there is a curse פסוק that names the belly before the thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the curse it is also written: "to make the belly swell and the thigh fall away"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer. Even within the curse, one פסוק puts the belly first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the curse goes thigh-first and only the water goes belly-first. But the words "לצבות בטן ולנפל ירך" are part of the curse the כהן says. So the curse itself seems to use both orders.

phrases.english: In the curse, too, it is written:
"to make the belly swell and the thigh fall away"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the curse always names the thigh first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק inside the curse names the belly first, so the curse is not consistently thigh-first

steps.title: That פסוק is the כהן warning her how the water will act
steps.stepSummary: The belly-first curse is the כהן telling her ahead of time the order in which the water will work, so nobody doubts the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is where the כהן lets her know that the belly comes first and then the thigh. This is so that people will not speak badly of the bitter water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The belly-first words are not the curse's order; they are information the כהן gives her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real curse is the thigh-first one. In the belly-first line, the כהן is explaining what the water will physically do. If he had said only 'thigh then belly' and the belly swelled first, people might think the water was not working properly.

keyTerms.meaning: to spread a bad name, cast doubt
the bitter water given to the סוטה

steps.whatToRemember: The curse names the thigh first (her sin began with the thigh). The water works belly first. The כהן tells her this order so no one doubts the water.

phrases.english: That is where the כהן informs her
that the belly comes first and then the thigh,
so as not to spread a bad name
about the bitter water.
phrases.notes: If the belly swelled first after he said 'thigh first', people might think the water was broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the function of the second פסוק: it informs her rather than curses her
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The belly-first line seemed to be part of the curse's order
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a warning about the water's physical order, said to protect the water's credibility

steps.title: שמשון followed his eyes and lost his eyes
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה gives another example of measure for measure: שמשון sinned with his eyes, so the פלשתים gouged them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: שמשון followed his eyes, so the פלשתים gouged out his eyes, as it says: "And the פלשתים seized him and gouged out his eyes."
steps.whatsHappening: We start a new משנה. It continues the theme of punishment that matches the sin, beginning with שמשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמשון chose wives based on what he saw, following his eyes. His punishment hit exactly that body part.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Samson followed his eyes;
therefore the Philistines gouged out his eyes,
as it is said:
"And the Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה continuing the measure-for-measure theme
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Punishment matches the sin: שמשון sinned with his eyes and lost his eyes

steps.title: אבשלום: hanged by his hair, ten spears for ten concubines
steps.stepSummary: אבשלום was proud of his hair and was hanged by it. He took his father's ten concubines and was struck by ten spears.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבשלום was proud of his hair, so he was hanged by his hair. And because he was with ten of his father's concubines, ten spears were put into him, as it says: "And ten young men, armor-bearers of יואב, surrounded him."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with אבשלום. It gives two matching punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hair he was proud of became the trap that caught him. The number ten matches too: ten concubines, ten spears.

phrases.english: Absalom was proud of his hair;
therefore he was hanged by his hair.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְפִי שֶׁבָּא עַל עֶשֶׂר פִּלַגְשֵׁי אָבִיו —
phrases.english: And because he had relations with ten concubines of his father,
therefore ten spears were put into him,
as it is said:
"And ten young men, Joab's armor-bearers, surrounded him."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 18:15. The פסוק goes on to say they struck him and killed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second example to the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבשלום's punishments matched his pride in his hair and his ten sins with the concubines

steps.title: Three stolen hearts, three spears in the heart
steps.stepSummary: אבשלום fooled three hearts: his father's, the court's and ישראל's. So three spears were thrust into his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: And because he stole three times, the heart of his father, the heart of the court and the heart of ישראל, as it says: "And אבשלום stole the heart of the men of ישראל," therefore three spears were thrust into him, as it says: "He took three spears in his hand and thrust them into the heart of אבשלום."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third matching punishment for אבשלום, again based on the number and the body part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Stealing a heart' means tricking someone. He tricked three hearts, so three spears went into his own heart.
steps.confusionAlert: In this פסוק, שבטים means spears or rods, not the tribes of ישראל.

phrases.english: And because he committed three thefts:

phrases.aramaic: לֵב אָבִיו, וְלֵב בֵּית דִּין, וְלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: the heart of his father, the heart of the court, and the heart of Israel,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְגַנֵּב אַבְשָׁלוֹם אֶת לֵב אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ —
phrases.english: as it is said: "And Absalom stole the heart of the men of Israel,"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 15:6. 'Stole the heart' means he fooled them and won them over.

phrases.english: therefore three spears were thrust into him,
as it is said:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיִּקַּח שְׁלֹשָׁה שְׁבָטִים בְּכַפּוֹ וַיִּתְקָעֵם בְּלֵב אַבְשָׁלוֹם״.
phrases.english: "And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the אבשלום example with a third matching punishment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three stolen hearts were matched by three spears in his heart

steps.title: Reward too: מרים waited for משה, so ישראל waited for her
steps.stepSummary: The same rule works for good deeds. מרים waited one hour for baby משה, so all ישראל waited seven days for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true for good: מרים waited for משה one hour, as it says: "And his sister stood from afar." Therefore ישראל waited for her seven days in the desert, as it says: "And the people did not travel until מרים was brought back."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns from punishment to reward. It shows that measure for measure also works for good deeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרים's small act, one hour of waiting by the river, was repaid with a much bigger honor: the whole nation waited a week.
steps.whatToRemember: מידה כנגד מידה works both ways: שמשון and אבשלום were punished to match their sins, and מרים was rewarded to match her kindness.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ה׳'s justice is not only about punishment. Good deeds are repaid in kind, and even more generously.

phrases.english: And so too regarding good:
Miriam waited for Moses one hour,
as it is said: "And his sister stood from afar";

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ נִתְעַכְּבוּ לָהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל שִׁבְעָה יָמִים בַּמִּדְבָּר,
phrases.english: therefore Israel waited for her seven days in the desert,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהָעָם לֹא נָסַע עַד הֵאָסֵף מִרְיָם״.
phrases.english: as it is said: "And the people did not travel until Miriam was brought back in."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the measure-for-measure rule from punishment to reward
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reward also matches the deed: מרים waited for משה, so ישראל waited for her

steps.title: יוסף buried his father, so משה carried יוסף
steps.stepSummary: יוסף gave his father יעקב a grand burial. In return he was cared for by משה, the greatest person there was.
steps.simpleTranslation: יוסף had the merit of burying his father, and none of his brothers was greater than him, as the פסוק says: "יוסף went up to bury his father, and chariots and horsemen went up with him." Who is greater to us than יוסף? Nobody less than משה took care of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another example of a good deed repaid measure for measure. יוסף honored his father's burial, and the greatest person, משה, honored יוסף's burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף was the most important brother, the ruler of מצרים, and he still took care of his father's burial himself. His reward matches the deed: the most important person in ישראל, משה, personally carried his remains. The chariots and horsemen in the פסוק show how great an honor יוסף gave his father.

keyTerms.meaning: took care of him, involved himself with him

phrases.english: Joseph merited to bury his father,
and there was none among his brothers greater than he,
as it is stated: "And Joseph went up to bury his father

phrases.aramaic: וַיַּעֲלוּ עִמּוֹ גַּם רֶכֶב גַּם פָּרָשִׁים״.
phrases.english: and there went up with him both chariots and horsemen."
phrases.notes: בראשית 50:9. The משנה skips ahead in the פסוקים to show how big the funeral was.

phrases.english: Who, to us, is greater than Joseph,
since none other than Moses took care of him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of good deeds rewarded measure for measure, which began with מרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because יוסף personally buried his father, the greatest person, משה, personally took care of יוסף's remains.

steps.title: משה carried יוסף's bones, so ה׳ buried משה
steps.stepSummary: משה took care of יוסף's bones. In return, ה׳ Himself buried משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה had the merit of taking יוסף's bones, and nobody in ישראל was greater than him, as it says: "משה took יוסף's bones with him." Who is greater than משה? Nobody but ה׳ took care of him, as it says: "And He buried him in the valley."
steps.whatsHappening: The chain of rewards goes one level higher. משה took care of יוסף's bones, so ה׳ Himself took care of משה's burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה, the greatest person in ישראל, personally took care of יוסף's bones. Since nobody is greater than משה, only ה׳ could repay him in kind, and the פסוק says ה׳ buried him.

keyTerms.meaning: a name for ה׳, literally "the Place"

phrases.english: Moses merited to take Joseph's bones,
and there was none in Israel greater than he,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף עִמּוֹ״
phrases.english: as it is stated: "And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him."
Who is greater than Moses,
since none other than the Omnipresent took care of him,
as it is stated: "And He buried him in the valley."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds directly on step 14. משה's care for יוסף is itself repaid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because משה personally carried יוסף's bones, ה׳ Himself buried משה.

steps.title: Not just משה: ה׳ gathers in all the צדיקים
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ taking part in burial is not only for משה. It is true for every צדיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not say this about משה alone, but about all צדיקים, as it says: "Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of ה׳ will gather you in."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה widens the idea from step 15. ה׳'s personal care at death belongs to all צדיקים, not only משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think ה׳ burying משה was a one-time honor. The פסוק in ישעיהו shows that "the glory of ה׳" gathers in every righteous person at their death.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule of מידה כנגד מידה works for good too: מרים, יוסף and משה were each rewarded in a way that matched their deed, and every צדיק is gathered in by ה׳'s glory.

phrases.english: Not about Moses alone did they say this,
but about all the righteous,
as it is stated: "And your righteousness shall go before you;
the glory of the Lord shall gather you in."

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא עַל מֹשֶׁה בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ, אֶלָּא עַל כׇּל הַצַּדִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens step 15's lesson to everyone righteous.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ takes part in gathering in every צדיק at death, not only משה.

steps.title: שמשון sinned with his eyes and lost his eyes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that proves from פסוקים that שמשון's sin was with his eyes, so his punishment was with his eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: שמשון rebelled with his eyes, as it says: "שמשון said to his father: Take her for me, because she is pleasing in my eyes." Therefore the פלשתים gouged out his eyes, as it says: "The פלשתים seized him and gouged out his eyes."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It brings a ברייתא that gives the פסוקים behind the משנה's line (step 10) about שמשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only stated that שמשון sinned with his eyes. This ברייתא shows the source: he chose a פלשתי wife because she looked good "in my eyes," and the punishment hit those same eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: she is pleasing in my eyes

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
Samson rebelled with his eyes,
as it is stated: "And Samson said to his father:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתָהּ קַח לִי כִּי הִיא יָשְׁרָה בְעֵינָי״
phrases.english: Get her for me, for she is pleasing in my eyes."
phrases.notes: שופטים 14:3. "Her" is the פלשתי woman שמשון wanted to marry.

phrases.english: Therefore the Philistines gouged out his eyes,
as it is stated: "And the Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא now begins and goes back to the משנה's שמשון example from step 10 to give its פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמשון sinned by following his eyes, so he was punished by losing his eyes.

steps.title: But the marriage came from God
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: a פסוק says שמשון's choice of wife came from ה׳, so how can it be called a sin?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But it is written: "His father and his mother did not know that it was from ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks step 17. If ה׳ arranged this marriage, it seems unfair to say שמשון sinned with his eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The very next פסוק after "she is pleasing in my eyes" says the match was from ה׳, as a way to get at the פלשתים. That suggests שמשון was carrying out ה׳'s plan and not chasing his own desires.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But isn't it written:
"And his father and his mother did not know
that it was from the Lord."
phrases.notes: שופטים 14:4, right after the פסוק quoted in the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמשון sinned with his eyes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says the match was from ה׳, so it seems שמשון was doing ה׳'s will and not sinning.

steps.title: שמשון still went after what he liked
steps.stepSummary: Even if ה׳ planned it, when שמשון actually went, he was following his own desire.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, when he went, he went after what was pleasing to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in step 18. ה׳'s plan does not excuse שמשון, because his own reason for going was what he liked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things are true at once. ה׳ used the marriage for His plan against the פלשתים. But שמשון's own motive was personal attraction, not a מצוה, and that motive is what he is judged for.

keyTerms.meaning: what was pleasing (straight) in his eyes

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not deny that the marriage was from ה׳. It is saying that ה׳'s plan and שמשון's personal motive are two separate things, and he is judged by his motive.
steps.whatToRemember: A person is judged by why he acts, even when his action ends up fitting into ה׳'s larger plan.

phrases.english: In any case, when he went,
he went after what was pleasing to him.
phrases.notes: Same root as "יָשְׁרָה בְעֵינָי" from the first פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲזַל מִיהָא בָּתַר יַשְׁרוּתֵיהּ אֲזַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates ה׳'s plan from the person's own motive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the match was from ה׳‎, שמשון did nothing wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳ planned the outcome, but שמשון's own motive was desire, so he is still blamed for sinning with his eyes.

steps.title: רבי: The Sin and the Punishment Were Both in עזה
steps.stepSummary: רבי teaches that שמשון's wrongdoing began in עזה, so he was punished in עזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says: His first wrongdoing was in עזה, so he was punished in עזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא from רבי about where שמשון's downfall began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the ברייתא matched the body part: he sinned with his eyes, so he was punished in his eyes. Now רבי matches the place: where the sin started is where the punishment came. This is the same idea of מדה כנגד מדה, applied to location.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi says:
His first wrongdoing was in Gaza,
therefore he was punished in Gaza.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: תְּחִילַּת קִלְקוּלוֹ בְּעַזָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא about שמשון, now matching the place of the sin to the place of the punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמשון's wrongdoing began in עזה, so his punishment came in עזה.

steps.title: The פסוקים That Show Both Halves Happened in עזה
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק shows he sinned in עזה, and another shows he was brought down to עזה as a prisoner.
steps.simpleTranslation: His first wrongdoing was in עזה, as it says: "And שמשון went to עזה and saw there a זונה." So he was punished in עזה, as it says: "And they brought him down to עזה."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now proves both parts of רבי's statement from פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק places the sin in עזה. The second פסוק places the punishment in עזה. Together they show the place of the sin matches the place of the punishment.

phrases.english: His first wrongdoing was in Gaza, as it is written:
"And Samson went to Gaza
and saw there a harlot, etc."
therefore he was punished in Gaza, as it is written:
"And they brought him down to Gaza."
phrases.notes: שופטים 16:21. That same פסוק tells how the פלשתים put out his eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוקים behind רבי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That the sin and the punishment were both in עזה.

steps.title: But Didn't It Start Earlier, in תמנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that שמשון went to תמנה before עזה, so maybe his wrongdoing really started there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: "And שמשון went down to תמנה"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי by bringing an earlier פסוק about תמנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story in תמנה, where he chose a פלשתי woman, comes before the story in עזה. If that was a wrongdoing, then עזה was not the first one. That would break רבי's statement.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"And Samson went down to Timnah"?
phrases.notes: שופטים 14:1. This happened before the עזה story, so the question is why עזה counts as the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim from step 20 that עזה was the start.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's claim that שמשון's wrongdoing began in עזה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תמנה episode comes earlier in the פסוקים, so it seems to be the true start.

steps.title: עזה Is Still the Real Start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the start of his actual wrongdoing was still in עזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, his first wrongdoing was in עזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא holds onto רבי's statement. Even though תמנה came first, the real wrongdoing began in עזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תמנה, שמשון at least married the woman he wanted. In עזה, the פסוק speaks of a זונה, with no marriage at all. So עזה stays the first real wrongdoing.

phrases.english: His first wrongdoing
in any case was in Gaza.
phrases.notes: "מיהא" means: whatever you say about תמנה, the real wrongdoing still began in עזה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about תמנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between the two episodes and keeps the original claim.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since תמנה came first, it should count as the start of his wrongdoing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The real start of his wrongdoing was in עזה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי teaches that שמשון was punished in the same place where his wrongdoing began, עזה. תמנה does not count as the start.

steps.title: דלילה's Name Fits What She Did
steps.stepSummary: רבי says that even if she had not been named דלילה, the name would fit her, because she weakened שמשון in three ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And afterward he loved a woman in the valley of שורק, and her name was דלילה." It was taught: רבי says: Even if her name had not been דלילה, she deserved to be called דלילה. She weakened his strength, she weakened his heart, and she weakened his deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the story, דלילה, and brings רבי's teaching about her name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads her name as a hint to the word דלדל, which means to weaken. He lists three things she weakened: his strength, his heart, and his deeds. The next step will prove each one.

keyTerms.meaning: even if not, had it not been

phrases.english: "And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman
in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah."
It was taught: Rabbi says:
Even if her name had not been called "Delilah,"
she deserved to be called Delilah:
she weakened his strength,
she weakened his heart,
she weakened his deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אִילְמָלֵא לֹא נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ ״דְּלִילָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves forward in the שמשון story to דלילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name דלילה fits her because she weakened שמשון's strength, heart, and deeds.

steps.title: Verses for the Three Ways She Weakened Him
steps.stepSummary: Each of the three weakenings is proven from a פסוק, ending with the שכינה leaving שמשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: She weakened his strength, as it says: "And his strength left him." She weakened his heart, as it says: "And דלילה saw that he had told her all his heart." She weakened his deeds, because the שכינה left him, as it says: "But he did not know that ה׳ had left him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves each of רבי's three points with a פסוק from the דלילה story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strength: his power left him. Heart: she got him to reveal his whole secret. Deeds: the worst loss, because the שכינה, which had helped him, left him, and he did not even notice.

keyTerms.meaning: he told her all his heart

phrases.english: She weakened his strength, as it is written:
"And his strength left him."
She weakened his heart, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַתֵּרֶא דְּלִילָה כִּי הִגִּיד לָהּ אֶת כׇּל לִבּוֹ״.
phrases.english: "And Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart."
She weakened his deeds,
for the Divine Presence departed from him,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְהוּא לֹא יָדַע כִּי ה׳ סָר מֵעָלָיו״.
phrases.english: as it is written: "But he did not know that the Lord had departed from him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves each of the three points listed in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That דלילה weakened שמשון's strength, heart, and deeds.
steps.whatToRemember: דלילה "weakened" שמשון in three ways: his strength left, his heart's secret came out, and the שכינה left him.

steps.title: How did דלילה know he told the truth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that דלילה saw he told her everything, and asks how she knew.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart." How did she know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק and asks how דלילה knew that this time שמשון was telling the truth. This sets up two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמשון had already lied to her several times about where his strength came from. So the question is real: what made this answer different? The next two steps give two different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: All his heart, meaning his full secret

phrases.english: "And Delilah saw that he had told her
all his heart."
From where did she know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the three weakenings of שמשון to another detail in the דלילה story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How דלילה could tell that שמשון was finally telling the truth.

steps.title: True words can be recognized
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין in the name of רב answers that words of truth are recognizable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנין said in the name of רב: Words of truth are recognizable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer: true words just sound true, so she could feel it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not point to any special detail in what שמשון said. It says truth has its own feel, and a listener can sense it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanin said in the name of Rav:
Words of truth are recognizable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She sensed it because true words have a recognizable quality.

steps.title: אביי: a צדיק would not use ה׳'s name for nothing
steps.stepSummary: אביי says she knew שמשון was a צדיק who would not mention שם שמים in vain, so when he said 'I am a נזיר of God' she knew it was true.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: She knew that this צדיק would not say the name of Heaven for nothing. Once he said, "I am a נזיר of God," she said: Now he is surely telling the truth.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second answer: this time שמשון used הקב"ה's name, and she knew he would never do that falsely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב, אביי points to a clear sign in the words themselves. In his earlier lies שמשון never mentioned הקב"ה. Once he said 'נזיר אלהים', she knew he must be serious.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of Heaven for no purpose, in vain

phrases.english: Abaye said:
She knew about that righteous man
that he would not bring out the name of Heaven for nothing.
Once he said, "I am a nazir of God,"
she said: Now he is surely telling the truth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same question, after רב's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She knew because he mentioned God's name, which a צדיק would never do falsely.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to how דלילה knew: רב says truth can be felt; אביי says the mention of הקב"ה's name proved it.

steps.title: What does 'and she pressed him' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that דלילה pressured שמשון and asks what the word 'ותאלצהו' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And it was, when she pressed him with her words all the days, and she urged him." What does "and she urged him" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another פסוק and asks what the extra word 'ותאלצהו' adds. This sets up רבי יצחק's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already said she pressured him with words every day. So 'and she urged him' seems to describe something more, and the גמרא wants to know what.

keyTerms.meaning: And she urged him, pushed him

phrases.english: "And it was, when she pressed him with her words
all the days, and she urged him."
What is "and she urged him"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase in the דלילה story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra pressure the word 'ותאלצהו' describes.

steps.title: How דלילה pushed him to reveal the secret
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי says she pulled away from him at the moment of intimacy, pressuring him to tell her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק from the school of רבי אמי said: At the time of finishing relations, she slipped out from under him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains that the 'urging' was physical: she pulled away from שמשון at a very intimate moment to pressure him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words alone had not worked. By withholding herself at that moment, she pushed him past his limit, which matches the end of the פסוק saying he was vexed to death.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יצחק of the study house of רבי אמי

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak of the house of Rabbi Ami said:
At the time of completing relations
she slipped away from beneath him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ותאלצהו' means she withdrew from him at the moment of intimacy.

steps.title: Why warn his mother not to eat anything unclean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the angel's warning to שמשון's mother and asks what 'כל טמא' means, since she surely never ate non-kosher food before.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Now be careful, please, do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean." What is "anything unclean"? And also: until now was she eating unclean things?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the angel's words and finds them strange: why tell a righteous woman not to eat non-kosher food? This sets up רבי יצחק's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ועתה' (now) suggests something new starts now. But she never ate forbidden food before either. So 'unclean' must mean something different here.

phrases.english: "And now, please be careful,
phrases.notes: שופטים 13:4, the angel speaking to שמשון's mother.

phrases.english: and do not drink wine or strong drink,
and do not eat anything unclean."
What is "anything unclean"?

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ: עַד הַשְׁתָּא דְּבָרִים טְמֵאִים קָאָכְלָה?!
phrases.english: And also: until now was she eating unclean things?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק about שמשון's birth.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain meaning of 'כל טמא' in the angel's warning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A righteous woman never ate non-kosher food, so warning her 'now' not to eat it makes no sense.

steps.title: Unclean means things forbidden to a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי explains that 'unclean' here means things forbidden to a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק from the school of רבי אמי said: Things that are forbidden to a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers that 'unclean' here means foods forbidden to a נזיר, since she was carrying a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grape products are normally permitted, so this is a real new warning. That fits 'now', and it fits right after the warning about wine.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak of the house of Rabbi Ami said:
Things that are forbidden to a nazir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Unclean' means non-kosher food, which makes the warning pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Unclean' means things a נזיר may not eat, which are new restrictions for her.

steps.title: Saved through an unclean thing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי says שמשון desired something unclean, so his life was saved through something unclean, the donkey's jawbone.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And God split open the hollow place in Lechi." רבי יצחק from the school of רבי אמי said: He desired something unclean, therefore his life depended on something unclean.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains that when שמשון nearly died of thirst, his water came from a donkey's jawbone, an unclean thing, because he had chased after something unclean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a מידה כנגד מידה lesson, like the earlier lessons about שמשון's eyes and עזה. He was drawn to פלשתי women, so even his rescue came through something unclean. It shows how a person's choices shape how הקב"ה deals with him.

keyTerms.meaning: The hollow place, like a socket
Jawbone, also the name of the place

steps.whatToRemember: שמשון's life is full of measure-for-measure: he wanted something unclean, so his rescue came through something unclean.

phrases.english: "And God split open the hollow place that is in Lechi."
phrases.notes: שופטים 15:19. Water came out of the donkey's jawbone he had fought with.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak of the house of Rabbi Ami said:
He desired something unclean —
therefore his life was made to depend on something unclean.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from the same רבי יצחק on a new פסוק about שמשון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because שמשון desired something unclean, his life was saved through something unclean, the donkey's jawbone.

steps.title: יעקב's prophecy about דן took effect through שמשון
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא reads 'ותחל' as 'took effect': יעקב אבינו's prophecy that דן would be like a snake came true through שמשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And the spirit of ה׳ began to move him.' רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: the prophecy of יעקב אבינו took effect, as it says, 'Dan shall be a serpent on the road.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new פסוק about שמשון, and רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains the word 'ותחל' in a deeper way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply read, 'ותחל' means the spirit 'began' to move שמשון. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא connects it to the word for 'coming to rest' or 'taking effect', and says יעקב's blessing to דן finally came true. שמשון was from שבט דן, and he fought the פלשתים alone, like a single snake attacking from the side of the road.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it began'. Here it is read as 'it took effect'.
Took effect, came to rest upon
A snake on the road. This is יעקב's blessing to דן.

phrases.english: "And the spirit of the Lord began, etc."
Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
The prophecy of Yaakov our father took effect,
phrases.notes: He reads 'ותחל' like 'חלתה', meaning something came to rest or came true.

phrases.english: as it is written: "Dan shall be a serpent on the road."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַתָּחֵל רוּחַ ה׳ וְגוֹ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the דלילה and jawbone teachings to explain a new פסוק about the start of שמשון's career.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ותחל' hints that יעקב's prophecy about דן being a snake came true through שמשון.

steps.title: The שכינה rang before שמשון like a bell
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי learns from 'לפעמו', which sounds like 'פעמון' (bell), that the שכינה rang before שמשון like a bell.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To move him in the camp of Dan.' רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי said: this teaches that the שכינה rang in front of him like a bell. It says here 'לפעמו', and it says there, about the כהן גדול's robe, 'a bell (פעמון) and a pomegranate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of the same פסוק. It proves its point by matching the word 'לפעמו' to the word 'פעמון' in another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לפעמו' usually means 'to stir him'. רבי יצחק דבי רבי אמי points out that it shares a root with 'פעמון', the bells on the כהן גדול's robe. So the spirit that stirred שמשון is pictured as the שכינה ringing before him like a bell.

keyTerms.meaning: To stir him or move him
'It is written here, and it is written there.' This is the way the גמרא links two פסוקים by a shared word.

phrases.english: "To move him in the camp of Dan,"

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak of the school of Rabbi Ami said:
This teaches that the Divine Presence
was ringing before him like a bell.
It is written here: "To move him in the camp of Dan,"
and it is written there: "A bell and a pomegranate."
phrases.notes: שמות 39:26. These are the bells on the hem of the כהן גדול's robe.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפַעֲמוֹ בְּמַחֲנֵה דָן אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק (שופטים 13:25), one phrase further.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה rang before שמשון like a bell, learned by linking 'לפעמו' to 'פעמון'.

steps.title: שמשון ground two mountains together
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי says צרעה and אשתאול were two huge mountains, and שמשון uprooted them and ground them against each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Between צרעה and אשתאול.' רבי אסי said: צרעה and אשתאול were two large mountains, and שמשון uprooted them and ground them one against the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last words of the פסוק. רבי אסי describes how strong שמשון was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק only gives the location where the spirit began to move שמשון. רבי אסי reads 'between' as describing an action: שמשון took the two mountains and ground them together. This shows his superhuman strength once the spirit came upon him.

keyTerms.meaning: צרעה and אשתאול. Two places named in the פסוק.

phrases.english: "Between Zorah and Eshtaol,"
Rabbi Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: צׇרְעָה וְאֶשְׁתָּאוֹל שְׁנֵי הָרִים גְּדוֹלִים הָיוּ,
phrases.english: Zorah and Eshtaol were two large mountains,
and Shimshon uprooted them and ground them one against the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין צׇרְעָה וּבֵין אֶשְׁתָּאוֹל אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the phrase-by-phrase reading of שופטים 13:25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צרעה and אשתאול were mountains that שמשון uprooted and ground together.
steps.whatToRemember: The three phrases of שופטים 13:25 each teach something about שמשון. 'ותחל' shows that יעקב's prophecy came true. 'לפעמו' shows the שכינה ringing like a bell. 'בין צרעה ובין אשתאול' shows his enormous strength.

steps.title: Introducing a teaching on 'and he shall begin to save Israel'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the angel's words that שמשון 'shall begin to save Israel' and introduces a teaching of רבי חמא ברבי חנינא. His actual words continue in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he shall begin to save ישראל.' רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next teaching. It quotes a new פסוק and names who will explain it, but the explanation itself comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only opens a new topic. The word 'יחל' looks like 'ותחל' from the earlier פסוק, so רבי חמא ברבי חנינא is about to comment on it as well. Wait for the next lines to see what he learns from it.

phrases.english: "And he shall begin to save Israel,"
phrases.notes: שופטים 13:5. These are the angel's words to שמשון's mother.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא יָחֵל לְהוֹשִׁיעַ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פסוק for explanation after finishing שופטים 13:25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A setup line: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא is about to explain 'והוא יחל להושיע את ישראל'.
